title: Figure 5.1. Before and after diagnostic-confidence rating distributions
objective: test the ease of diagnosis of acute appendicitis among resident doctors and medical officers using the combined MAS and hsCRP

notes: Complete paired ordinal ratings: 36; incomplete/invalid pairs: 0.
Before: independent clinical confidence without MAS/hsCRP. After: confidence after receiving both. Same clinician within each patient pair is confirmed.
Clinician identity/repeated-case clustering and resident/medical-officer group are unavailable; no independence across cases or professional-group inference is assumed.
Confidence is a proxy, not a direct ease-of-diagnosis item or proof of improved diagnostic accuracy.
Loaded records: 36; result-level analysis n: 36. Row-specific denominators take precedence where shown.

CI = confidence interval; SD = standard deviation; Q1–Q3 = first to third quartile (IQR limits); n = number of observations. Not estimable/Not estimated identifies unavailable evidence; Not applicable identifies an irrelevant field.
Figure sample size and axis units follow the actual plotted observations and stated source definitions.
result.interpretation: These results address recorded confidence after MAS/hsCRP information; confidence does not establish diagnostic accuracy. Not confident at all: before 8, after 7, using the same 36 complete pairs. Slightly confident: before 7, after 8, using the same 36 complete pairs. Moderately confident: before 7, after 7, using the same 36 complete pairs. Further series are displayed in the figure; the examples above are in display order and are not a ranking. Before and after distributions use the same complete pairs.
result.precision: Unrounded stored statistics appear in the calculation log where available; displayed estimates are rounded. Descriptive cells without an underlying logged summary retain their displayed precision. Retained reporting convention α = 0.05; 95% intervals. Protocol prespecification must be confirmed. Explicitly added analyses remain exploratory. All new tests exploratory unless explicitly supported by the approved objective.
